understood.claimRestated: Water always boils at 100 degrees everywhere.

subClaims.missingEvidence: A physics reference giving the boiling point of water and the pressure at which it was measured.
subClaims.backgroundNote: Pure water boils at about 100 °C at normal atmospheric pressure (at sea level). General knowledge, not evidence.

subClaims.text: This is true everywhere (even in the mountains).
subClaims.missingEvidence: Measurements of the boiling point at different altitudes, or a reference on how pressure affects boiling point.
subClaims.backgroundNote: At high altitude the air pressure is lower and water boils below 100 °C. This is a general note, not evidence, and it shows why the "everywhere" part must be checked on its own.

caveats: This claim has two parts: the boiling temperature, and "everywhere". The second part needs checking.
